title: Longest Increasing Run
problem: The first line of input is a positive integer N. The second line holds N integers separated by spaces. Print the length of the longest unbroken run of numbers where each one is strictly bigger than the one before it. For example, in 1 2 5 3 4 the longest run is 1 2 5, so the answer is 3. A single number is a run of length 1.
starter_code:
# The first line is N, the count of numbers.
# The second line holds N integers separated by spaces.
# Print the length of the longest strictly increasing run of neighbours.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Look at each number next to the one before it, and keep a running length of the current climb.
hints.2: Loop from the second number on. If it is bigger than the one before it, the current run grows by one; otherwise a new run starts at length 1. Keep the best length seen and update it after every number, so a run that reaches the end still counts. Equal numbers end a run.
hints.3:
input()
v = list(map(int, input().split()))
best = cur = 1
for i in range(1, len(v)):
    cur = cur + 1 if v[i] > v[i - 1] else 1
    best = max(best, cur)
print(best)

failure_explanation: The run must be strictly increasing and unbroken: two equal numbers in a row end it. Count numbers, not steps between them (a run of three numbers has length 3), update the best length after every number so a run that lasts to the end is counted, and compare the values as numbers so negative numbers work.
